facts: Two figures are **similar** when their matching angles are equal and their matching sides are all in the same ratio.
Any two right-angled triangles containing the same angle $\theta$ are similar, because their angles match: $90^{\circ}$, $\theta$, and $180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-\theta$.
Enlarging by a scale factor $k$ multiplies **both** lengths in a ratio by $k$, and the factor cancels: $\dfrac{kb}{kc}=\dfrac{b}{c}$.
So $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$ and $\tan\theta$ depend **only on the angle** $\theta$, never on how big the triangle is.
Change the **size** of the triangle and the ratios stay the same; change the **angle** and the ratios change.
The hypotenuse is the longest side, so $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ are always between $0$ and $1$.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Relative to $\theta$, the vertical side is opposite, the horizontal side is adjacent and the sloping side is the hypotenuse.
Triangle A:
$\begin{align*}\sin\theta&=\frac{10}{26}=\frac{5}{13}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{24}{26}=\frac{12}{13}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{10}{24}=\frac{5}{12}\end{align*}$
Triangle B:
$\begin{align*}\sin\theta&=\frac{15}{39}=\frac{5}{13}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{36}{39}=\frac{12}{13}\\\tan\theta&=\frac{15}{36}=\frac{5}{12}\end{align*}$
Their matching angles are equal and their corresponding sides are proportional. Every side of B is $1.5$ times the corresponding side of A. This common factor cancels in each ratio, so all three ratios agree.

workedExamples.question_text: A right-angled triangle has $\cos\theta=\frac{11}{61}$. Every side is multiplied by $0.2$. Find the new cosine ratio and explain why it is unchanged.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Cosine compares the adjacent side with the hypotenuse. Both lengths are multiplied by the same factor:
$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{0.2\times11}{0.2\times61}\\&=\frac{2.2}{12.2}\\&=\frac{11}{61}\end{align*}$
The factor $0.2$ cancels. Scaling preserves the angles, so the cosine ratio is unchanged. The same cancellation applies to sine and tangent.

The side labelled $x$ is adjacent to $60^{\circ}$; the hypotenuse is $23.4\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}\cos60^{\circ}&=\frac{x}{23.4}\\\frac{x}{23.4}&=\frac12\\x&=23.4\times\frac12\\x&=11.7\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
The fixed cosine ratio applies regardless of the triangle's size.

$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac9{15}=\frac35\\\cos\phi&=\frac{12}{15}=\frac45\end{align*}$
The ratios differ because $\theta$ and $\phi$ are different angles. A trigonometric ratio is fixed by the angle, rather than the size of the triangle.

workedExamples.question_text: A right-angled triangle contains a $45^{\circ}$ angle. Its adjacent side is $8\text{ cm}$. Use $\tan45^{\circ}=1$ to find the opposite side and explain why every right-angled triangle containing $45^{\circ}$ is isosceles.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Let the opposite side be $b\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}\tan45^{\circ}&=\frac b8\\\frac b8&=1\\b&=8\end{align*}$
Both shorter sides are $8\text{ cm}$, so this triangle is isosceles.
For any right-angled triangle containing $45^{\circ}$, $\frac{O}{A}=1$, so $O=A$. Its two shorter sides are equal regardless of its size.

workedExamples.question_text:
Explain why none of these ratios can describe an acute angle $\theta$ in a right-angled triangle:
(a) $\sin\theta=1.25$
(b) $\tan\theta=-0.4$
(c) $\cos\theta=0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $\sin\theta=\frac OH=1.25$ would require $O=1.25H$. The opposite side would exceed the hypotenuse, which must be the longest side.
(b) $\tan\theta=\frac OA$. Both lengths are positive, so their ratio cannot be negative.
(c) $\cos\theta=\frac AH=0$ would require $A=0$. A triangle cannot have a side of zero length.

development.question_text:
A right-angled triangle has $\cos\theta=\dfrac{7}{25}$.
Every side is multiplied by $0.4$.
Write $\cos\theta$ for the new triangle and explain your answer.
development.solution_text:
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{0.4\times 7}{0.4\times 25}$
$=\dfrac{2.8}{10}$
$=\dfrac{7}{25}$
Both the adjacent side and the hypotenuse are multiplied by $0.4$, so the factor cancels and the ratio is unchanged.

mastery.question_text:
In every right-angled triangle containing a $45^{\circ}$ angle, $\tan 45^{\circ}=1$.
Use this to explain why every such triangle is isosceles.
mastery.solution_text:
$\tan 45^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{Opp}}{\text{Adj}}=1$
so $\text{Opp}=\text{Adj}$.
The two shorter sides are equal in every right-angled triangle containing $45^{\circ}$, so every one of them is isosceles.

mastery.question_text: Explain why no right-angled triangle can have $\sin\theta=1.2$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{Opp}}{\text{Hyp}}=1.2$ would need $\text{Opp}=1.2\times\text{Hyp}$.
That makes the opposite side longer than the hypotenuse, but the hypotenuse is always the longest side of a right-angled triangle.
No such triangle exists, so $\sin\theta$ can never be greater than $1$.

mastery.question_text:
A right-angled triangle has $\cos\theta=\dfrac{9}{41}$.
Every side is multiplied by $0.125$.
What is the new cosine ratio? Explain your answer.
mastery.solution_text:
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{0.125\times 9}{0.125\times 41}$
$=\dfrac{1.125}{5.125}$
$=\dfrac{9}{41}$
Both the adjacent side and the hypotenuse are multiplied by $0.125$, so the factor cancels. The triangle is smaller, but its angles and cosine ratio are unchanged.

mastery.question_text: Explain why it is impossible for an angle $\theta$ in a right-angled triangle to have $\tan\theta=-0.75$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\text{Opp}}{\text{Adj}}$.
Both side lengths are positive, so their ratio must be positive.
A ratio of $-0.75$ would require one of these lengths to be negative, which is impossible.
